description: Diagnostic rules for the 32 astronaut health conditions (deep-space missions). Decision support only: every output is a suspicion or an alert level, never a confirmed diagnosis. Drug doses are terrestrial references and always require an approved mission SOP / crew medical officer.

conventions.signal_reference: A leaf {signal, level} points to thresholds.json -> signals.<signal>.<level> (e.g. spo2.caution_below). Numeric values are NOT duplicated here, so thresholds.json stays the single source of truth.
conventions.derived_signal_reference: A leaf {signal, operator, value, unit} compares a derived or manually entered measurement that is NOT in thresholds.json (see input_vocabulary.derived_signals). Operators: gte, gt, lte, lt.
conventions.expression_nodes: all = AND, any = OR, not = NOT, at_least = {n, of:[...]} (at least n of the listed leaves).
conventions.levels: rule.levels maps an alert level to the expression that triggers it. Evaluate from the highest suggested_priority downwards; ENVIRONMENT_ALERT and TEAM_SUPPORT are separate channels with no priority.
conventions.supporting_evidence: Optional expression that strengthens suspicion but is not required to trigger the level.
conventions.red_flags: Optional expression that excludes the benign classification and requires medical evaluation. The source sheet does not define an alert level for these cases.
conventions.incidence: Incidence values are modeled NASA CliFF rates (episodes per person-year), NOT probabilities, and none is validated for Mars DRM.
conventions.severity_markers: Informational markers from thresholds.json condition_cutoffs; they do not change the alert level.

alert_levels.meaning: Log the event and observe; no immediate intervention required.
Condition suspected from reported symptoms / context; clinical confirmation required.
Immediate intervention and activation of the crew medical team.
Habitat / environmental limit exceeded; independent of any symptom.
Non-medical team-support event; not a medical diagnosis.

symptoms.dangerous_behavior: Dangerous behavior / risk to self or others

context.chemical_eye_exposure_reported: Reported chemical exposure of the eye
context.foreign_particle_history: History of a particle entering the eye
context.gravity_re_exposure: Recent re-exposure to gravity (Moon / Mars / Earth landing)
context.local_co2_accumulation: Local CO2 accumulation / poorly mixed air area

core_temperature.label: Core body temperature (NOT available in thresholds.json: needs a core thermometer or manual entry)

watery_stool_count_24h.label: Watery stools in the last 24 h

diagnostic_rules.name: Mild/moderate allergic reaction
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No dedicated numeric indicator from the 6 sensors. HR/BP/SpO2: check for deterioration.

supporting_signals.purpose: Monitor for deterioration / progression to anaphylaxis
Monitor for deterioration / progression to anaphylaxis
Monitor for deterioration / progression to anaphylaxis

diagnostic_rules.logic_description: (Itching OR rash) AND possible exposure AND NO signs of anaphylaxis -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 characteristic symptom + exposure context. Not a definitive diagnosis.

timing.description: Any time after exposure (often minutes to hours).

recommended_steps: Check airway, breathing and blood pressure.
Inform the medically responsible crew member.

medication.summary: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine only if pre-approved; dose per mission SOP.

do_not: Do NOT use an antihistamine as a substitute for epinephrine if dyspnea, tongue swelling or hypotension is present.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: ~0.3293 episodes per person-year (modeled rate, NOT a 32.93% probability).

related_rules.relation: Escalate here if signs of anaphylaxis appear

diagnostic_rules.name: Anaphylaxis
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Possible hypotension/tachycardia or hypoxemia, with no mandatory numeric cut-off. A normal SpO2 does NOT exclude anaphylaxis.

supporting_signals.purpose: Hypoxemia may be present; normal value does not exclude

diagnostic_rules.logic_description: (Acute respiratory distress OR airway edema OR collapse/severe hypotension) with suspected allergic cause -> EMERGENCY. Rash is NOT required.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 critical clinical symptom/finding is enough for immediate intervention; not a confirmed diagnosis by the algorithm.

timing.description: Minutes to hours after exposure; any flight phase.

confirmation: Clinical criteria for anaphylaxis assessed by a trained crew member, not an automatic diagnosis from sensors
recommended_steps: Call the crew medical team and activate the emergency SOP.
Immediate IM epinephrine into the lateral thigh.
Supine/safe position depending on breathing; oxygen if required and available.
Continuous reassessment; IV fluids only by trained personnel.

medication.summary: IM epinephrine per approved mission SOP (general CDC clinical guidance, NOT a NASA Mars dose).

specific_dose.basis: General CDC guidance for terrestrial adults; requires approved mission SOP

do_not: Do NOT delay epinephrine for measurements or communication.
Do NOT use antihistamines/steroids as first-line treatment.
There is no absolute contraindication to IM epinephrine in true anaphylaxis.
medical_kit: Auto-injector or 1 mg/mL epinephrine with suitable syringe

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: 0.0004065 episodes/person-year (male), 0.0005902 (female), based mostly on terrestrial data; no recorded case during spaceflight.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: Dose and repeat interval come from CDC guidance for terrestrial adults; an approved mission SOP is required.

related_rules.relation: Rash with dyspnea/airway edema escalates here

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation low back pain
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: The 6 sensors do not diagnose back pain; HR/BP/SpO2 only to look for an alternative cause if accompanying symptoms exist.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Low back pain AND transition to microgravity AND no trauma/neurological red flags -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 main symptom + time context.

red_flags.description: Leg weakness, perineal numbness, loss of urinary control, or trauma: exclude simple back pain and request medical evaluation (alert level not defined in the source sheet).

timing.description: Most often during the initial days of microgravity; NOT an exclusive time limit.

typical_window.meaning: Typical onset window, first 2-5 days of flight (thresholds.json condition_cutoffs)

medication.summary: Analgesic only from the approved formulary, with no arbitrary dose.

do_not: Do NOT label as simple back pain if leg weakness, perineal numbness, loss of urinary control or trauma is present.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation constipation
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific numeric indicator from the 6 sensors.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Reduced bowel movements AND hard stools/straining after transition to microgravity -> SUSPECTED (source logic text); the source status column sets the event level to MONITOR.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 compatible symptoms (suggested software logic, not a NASA diagnostic rule).

red_flags.description: Severe abdominal pain, vomiting, significant distension or inability to pass gas: no laxative without assessment; exclude obstruction.

timing.description: Typically in the first 5-7 days; may occur later.

confirmation: History of bowel movements, fluids, diet, medications

medication.summary: Laxative from the approved kit; NASA CliFF does not document a safe individualized dose here.

do_not: Do NOT give a laxative or fiber without assessment when severe abdominal pain, vomiting, significant distension or inability to pass gas is present.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

related_rules.relation: Overlap: use one event code with a subtype, not two independent diagnoses

diagnostic_rules.name: CO2-related headache

escalation.when: CO2 limit exceeded on its own (no symptom required).

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Air ppCO2: rolling 1-hour mean > 3 mmHg -> environmental exceedance per NASA-STD-3001, NOT a headache diagnostic threshold. HR/BP/SpO2 for other causes.
typical_symptoms: Possible discomfort worsening in poor ventilation
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Headache AND high ppCO2 / local accumulation -> SUSPECTED; CO2 limit exceeded alone -> ENVIRONMENT ALERT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 symptom + 1 environmental evidence for suspicion. The environmental alert does not require a symptom.

timing.description: Any time, especially in areas with poor air mixing.

medication.summary: Analgesic only if pre-approved; CO2 correction takes priority over symptomatic treatment.

do_not: Do NOT assume ppCO2 equals PaCO2.
Do NOT dismiss the environmental alert with a painkiller.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: mean modeled rate 0.686 episodes/person-year under specific CO2 conditions; NOT a 68.6% probability.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: The 3 mmHg limit is a 1-hour air average, not a clinical diagnostic limit.

related_rules.relation: Adaptation headache; CO2 used to exclude an environmental cause

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation headache
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific numeric criterion. CO2 is used to check an alternative environmental cause.

supporting_signals.purpose: Rule out an alternative environmental cause

typical_symptoms: New headache after transition to microgravity
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Headache AND recent transition to microgravity AND no red flags, with CO2 assessment -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 symptom + phase / exclusion check.

red_flags.description: Sudden/thunderclap headache or new neurological symptom: not an adaptation headache.

timing.description: Most often in the first 5-7 days; no absolute exclusion afterwards.

medication.summary: Analgesic per mission formulary; specific dose not verified.

do_not: Do NOT automatically attribute sudden extremely severe headache or a new neurological symptom to microgravity.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation nasal congestion
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific rule from the 6 sensors. Core temperature (not skin temperature) is useful for possible infection.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Nasal congestion after onset of microgravity -> MONITOR; high fever / severe dyspnea -> different assessment.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 symptom for monitoring, not a specific diagnosis.

red_flags.description: High fever or severe dyspnea: evaluate for another cause.

timing.description: Most often early in flight, not an absolute window.

severity_markers.meaning: Worst case: complete obstruction needing 72-168 h (3-7 days) of treatment. Best case: 0-72 h.

confirmation: History of allergy, runny nose, accompanying infection symptoms

medication.summary: Saline nasal solution; decongestant only per SOP.

do_not: Do NOT use topical vasoconstrictors for a prolonged period without checking contraindications (e.g. hypertension).

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Space motion sickness
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific number. HR/BP and SpO2 only support screening for dehydration / other causes. QTc matters before ondansetron.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Nausea OR vomiting after entering microgravity, no red flags -> SUSPECTED. Continuous vomiting with dehydration -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 typical symptom + time context; not a definitive diagnosis.

red_flags.description: New focal neurological deficit: do not attribute to space motion sickness.

timing.description: Onset mainly in the first hours/days; usually resolves within 72-96 h, not a hard cut-off.

typical_window.meaning: Usually resolves within 72-96 h; not a hard cut-off

severity_markers.meaning: IMM worst case: more than 2 vomiting episodes (thresholds.json signals.vomiting_episodes).
Worst case: severe and persistent symptoms lasting over 72 h.

recommended_steps: Check for persistent or atypical symptoms.

medication.summary: Ondansetron or another approved antiemetic; DOSE ONLY from mission SOP (QT factors, interactions).

do_not: Do NOT give ondansetron automatically without checking QT prolongation / interactions.
Do NOT attribute new focal neurological deficits to space motion sickness.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: reports up to ~60% of crew members in historical observations; estimate from heterogeneous data with limitations, not a Mars-specific prediction.

numeric.unit: fraction of crew (upper bound, historical observations)

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation urinary incontinence
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: None of the six measurements is specific.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Involuntary leakage -> MONITOR / medical evaluation; in parallel check for dysuria and retention.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 reported leakage is enough to log an event.

timing.description: During initial adaptation or at any time.

severity_markers.meaning: Moderate to severe course: clinical phase II lasts 24-120 h. Best case: 0-24 h.

confirmation: Exclude UTI, voiding difficulty, overflow from retention

medication.summary: No automatic medication.

do_not: Do NOT give anticholinergic drugs without excluding urinary retention.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Space-adaptation urinary retention
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR/BP may change from pain, not specifically. No specific numeric limit.
typical_symptoms: Inability to urinate despite strong urge
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Inability to urinate WITH painful distension -> URGENT. Retention may exist without intense pain.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 main symptom is enough for immediate assessment, not clinical confirmation.

timing.description: Any time; space adaptation especially early.

severity_markers.meaning: Needs repeated or indwelling catheterization: 24-120 h. Best case: 0-24 h. Catheterization failure risk under 1% may require medical evacuation.

recommended_steps: Decompression by catheterization only by a trained person and per SOP.

medication.summary: No automatic treatment; options only from a physician.

do_not: Do NOT force large fluid intake when the patient cannot urinate.
Do NOT attempt catheterization without training / sterile kit.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

related_rules.relation: Incontinence may be overflow from retention

diagnostic_rules.name: Chemical eye injury
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: None of the 6 measurements identifies a chemical eye burn.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Reported chemical eye exposure -> EMERGENCY without waiting for any other sign.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 exposure event is enough to trigger emergency management.

timing.description: Immediately after the incident, any day.

confirmation: Ocular surface pH if available (after irrigation has started)
recommended_steps: IMMEDIATE copious irrigation with a suitable fluid.
Remove contact lenses if easily done.
Recheck pH / continue irrigation per SOP.

medication.summary: Topical drugs only after irrigation and by the physician; dose pending.

do_not: Do NOT delay irrigation to collect data.
Do NOT neutralize chemically with an acid or base.
Do NOT rub the eye.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Corneal abrasion
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific value from the 6 sensors.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Pain / foreign-body sensation WITH tearing / photophobia after a mechanical event -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 main + 1 accompanying symptom for suspicion; definitive assessment by examination.

timing.description: Any time after a mechanical event.

medication.summary: Topical antibiotic / analgesic only per SOP; doses not confirmed.

do_not: Do NOT let the patient repeatedly use topical anesthetics.
Do NOT give steroids without an ophthalmologist.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Eye foreign body

escalation.when: Penetrating injury suspected or vision reduced.

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific numeric threshold.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: History of a particle AND persistent foreign-body sensation -> SUSPECTED; penetrating injury / reduced vision -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 event/symptom is enough for assessment, not confirmation.

timing.description: Immediately after the event.

confirmation: Examination of eyelids / cornea by trained personnel
recommended_steps: Careful irrigation if penetration is not suspected.

medication.summary: No automatic medication; analgesia / antibiotic if the physician decides.

do_not: Do NOT remove an embedded object.
Do NOT press or rub the eye.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Orthostatic intolerance after transition to gravity
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Symptoms when upright +/- systolic BP drop >= 20 mmHg or diastolic drop >= 10 mmHg within 3 min: TERRESTRIAL criterion for orthostatic hypotension, NOT validated on Mars. HR for tachycardia.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: (Symptoms on standing AND improvement when lying down) -> SUSPECTED; BP drop strengthens suspicion; syncope -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 syncope for emergency; otherwise 1 typical symptom + orthostatic context.

timing.description: On re-exposure to gravity (Moon / Mars / Earth); not a general term for everyday flight.

confirmation: Safe orthostatic test protocol by trained personnel
Do not generalize the lunar 1/6 g CliFF to Mars 0.38 g
recommended_steps: Lie the patient down in a safe position.
Fluids / compression garments per the pre-approved landing plan.

medication.summary: Fluids (PO or IV) and anything else only per the planned flight SOP, with no automatic dose.

do_not: Do NOT allow upright work / EVA when dizzy or after syncope.
Do NOT force an orthostatic test on an unstable patient.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF lunar gravity-well: modeled mean 0.07191 per person (~7.2%) with 0 observed cases in 12 Apollo astronauts; do NOT use as a probability on Mars.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: 20/10 mmHg within 3 minutes is a terrestrial criterion and does not prove the diagnosis at 0.38 g.

diagnostic_rules.name: General constipation

escalation.when: Severe pain or vomiting (also distension or inability to pass gas).

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific value from the 6.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: >=2 symptoms of changed habits -> MONITOR/SUSPECTED; severe pain or vomiting -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 symptoms for suspicion (software logic, not NASA criteria).

timing.description: Any time, independent of microgravity adaptation.

medication.summary: Only per mission SOP.

do_not: Do NOT treat as simple constipation if there is intense pain, distended abdomen, inability to pass gas or continuous vomiting.

incidence.summary: No separate reliable value found for the general form. Do NOT double-count with C04.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: Overlaps with C04: use one event code with a subtype, not two independent diagnoses. Source reference is NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF, although the sheet links the space-adaptation constipation CliFF.

related_rules.relation: Overlap: one event code with a subtype

source.reference: NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF

diagnostic_rules.name: Acute diarrhea

escalation.when: Severe: blood in stool, syncope or hypotension.

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR/BP: possible sign of fluid loss (not specific). Core temperature for infection if available (skin temperature is not sufficient).
typical_symptoms: Possible fever or blood in stool
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: >=3 watery stools/24 h -> SUSPECTED acute diarrhea; blood, syncope, hypotension -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 main clinical criterion (>=3/24 h); not an etiological diagnosis.

timing.description: Any time; duration is recorded in hours/days.

recommended_steps: Monitor number of stools, BP and urine output.
Escalate when blood / fever / hypotension appear.

medication.summary: ORS as first-line management. Antidiarrheals/antibiotics only after assessment and per SOP; no recorded dose.

do_not: Do NOT give routine antibiotics.
Do NOT use antiperistaltics uncontrolled in bloody diarrhea or high fever.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: modeled mean rate ~0.92 episodes/person-year (NOT a 92% probability).

diagnostic_rules.name: Indigestion (dyspepsia)

escalation.when: Chest pain (especially with dyspnea / sweating or hemodynamic change); do not ignore hematemesis / melena.

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific metric; HR/BP/SpO2 help only if chest or severe symptoms are present.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Meal-related epigastric discomfort AND no signs of serious disease -> MONITOR.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 main symptom + relation to meals; not a diagnosis.

timing.description: Any time; related to meals.

confirmation: History of cardiovascular pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, vomiting

medication.summary: Antacid or other gastroprotective only from an approved kit, with no arbitrary dosing.

do_not: Do NOT label chest pain with dyspnea/sweating or hemodynamic change as indigestion.
Do NOT ignore hematemesis / melena.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: Available NASA CliFF is an older version (2020); no therapeutic dose is documented.

diagnostic_rules.name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)

escalation.when: Systemic signs: fever, chills, flank pain or hypotension.

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: CORE temperature >= 38 C is a general clinical sign of fever (not UTI-specific). HR/BP for severe systemic deterioration.
typical_symptoms: Fever / flank pain for possible pyelonephritis
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Dysuria AND (frequency OR urgency) -> SUSPECTED. Fever/chills/flank pain or hypotension -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 urological symptoms for suspicion. Laboratory confirmation where feasible.

timing.description: Any time.

recommended_steps: Antibiotic only with the mission physician protocol and allergy / resistance history.

medication.summary: Antibiotic and dose DEPEND on sex, UTI type, renal function, pregnancy, allergies and culture. No universal dose is defined.

do_not: Do NOT start an antibiotic automatically from fever alone.
Do NOT use incompatible / allergenic antibiotics without checking.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: modeled rate ~0.858 episodes/person-year under model assumptions; NOT an 85.8% individual probability.

diagnostic_rules.name: Vaginal yeast infection (vulvovaginal candidiasis)
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: The six sensors do not diagnose candidiasis; fever requires evaluation for another cause.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Itching AND characteristic discharge/redness -> SUSPECTED; confirm before specific treatment if in doubt.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 compatible symptoms for suspicion; not a confirmed diagnosis.

timing.description: Any time.

recommended_steps: Choose a topical azole if approved.

medication.summary: Terrestrial CDC guidance for confirmed uncomplicated VVC in a non-pregnant patient: fluconazole 150 mg PO once, OR a topical azole per regimen. NOT automatic space prescribing.

specific_dose.repeat: Single dose (or topical azole per regimen)
specific_dose.basis: CDC terrestrial guidance for confirmed uncomplicated VVC in non-pregnant patients; eligibility check required

do_not: AVOID oral fluconazole in pregnancy.
Check liver disease, interactions and QT before a systemic azole.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: 0.2553 episodes/person-year in the model for the relevant female population; NOT a 25.53% general crew probability.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: The 150 mg dose comes from terrestrial CDC guidance and requires an eligibility check.

diagnostic_rules.name: Bacterial skin infection / cellulitis
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Fever with CORE temperature >= 38 C may coexist; high HR / low BP in sepsis; not a specific diagnostic limit.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Redness AND (local pain OR warmth/swelling) with spread -> SUSPECTED. Fever with hypotension/confusion -> EMERGENCY (sepsis).
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 local findings for suspicion; one systemic red flag triggers escalation.

timing.description: Any time, often after skin injury.

recommended_steps: Mark the redness border / photograph (with consent).

medication.summary: Systemic or topical antibiotics according to severity, pathogen, allergies and mission SOP; no universal dosing.

do_not: Do NOT use steroids alone on a suspected infection.
Do NOT delay treatment of possible sepsis.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: ~0.2315 episodes/person-year in the model, not a 23.15% individual probability.

diagnostic_rules.name: Superficial skin abrasion
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: A numeric measurement from the 6 sensors is neither needed nor diagnostic.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Visible superficial abrasion after injury -> SUSPECTED / wound to treat.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 visible wound activates care.

timing.description: Immediately after the event.

confirmation: Depth, foreign bodies, contamination, vaccination history
recommended_steps: Wash / clean with a suitable fluid.

medication.summary: Topical treatment only per mission wound-care SOP; no dose needed if no drug is used.

do_not: Do NOT repeatedly apply irritant solutions inside the wound.
Do NOT overlook a foreign body.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Laceration / skin cut
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR/BP may indicate blood loss in severe bleeding but do not determine the type of wound.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Visible wound -> SUSPECTED / treat; uncontrolled bleeding OR syncope -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 wound/sign is enough for action; 2 of 3 are not required.

timing.description: Any time after injury.

recommended_steps: Clinical assessment for closure by trained personnel.

medication.summary: Local anesthetic / antibiotic only from the approved trauma SOP.

do_not: Do NOT close a deep or dirty wound without examination.
Do NOT remove an embedded object if there is a bleeding risk.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Skin rash

escalation.when: Dyspnea or airway edema (route to C02).

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR/BP/SpO2 only to check for a systemic allergic reaction. No quantitative rash criterion.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Visible rash -> MONITOR, ask about a trigger; dyspnea or airway edema -> C02 EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 visible symptom for an event; not a specific diagnosis.

red_flags.description: Mucosal lesions, fever or dyspnea: do not treat as a simple rash.

timing.description: Any time, after new drugs, chemicals or a change in environment.

confirmation: Differential: allergy, infection, irritant dermatitis, drug reaction
recommended_steps: Escalate if extensive, painful, with fever / mucous membranes.

medication.summary: Antihistamine or topical drug only if the cause is documented, with no specific dose.

do_not: Do NOT give systemic cortisone blindly.
Do NOT ignore a rash with mucosal lesions, fever or dyspnea.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Neurovestibular disorder on re-exposure to gravity

escalation.when: New focal neurological deficit (sudden weakness, diplopia, dysarthria, severe new headache).

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specialized measurement from the six; BP/HR check for a coexisting orthostatic cause.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Recent transition to gravity AND (vertigo OR unsteadiness) -> SUSPECTED; new focal neurological deficit -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 neurovestibular symptom + landing phase.

timing.description: Immediately on re-exposure to gravity and during initial adaptation.

confirmation: Nystagmus / balance check by trained personnel
recommended_steps: Progressive mobilization / vestibular rehabilitation per SOP.

medication.summary: Antiemetic only if approved; dose not documented.

do_not: Do NOT automatically treat sudden weakness, diplopia, dysarthria or severe new headache as ordinary vertigo.

incidence.summary: NASA CliFF: modeled value ~0.07191 per person in the specific lunar re-exposure; transfer of this % to Mars 0.38 g is NOT documented.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: Specific CliFF for the transition to lunar gravity. Do not derive a Mars probability.

diagnostic_rules.name: General headache

escalation.when: Any red flag (thunderclap onset, new neurological abnormality, neck stiffness with fever).

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR/BP/SpO2/CO2 as supporting checks. ppCO2 1 h > 3 mmHg checks an environmental factor. No numeric cut-off proves a headache type.
typical_symptoms: Headache; ask about sudden onset, severity, visual and neurological symptoms
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Headache -> MONITOR / clinical classification; thunderclap OR new neurological abnormality OR neck stiffness with fever -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 symptom to record. 1 red flag is enough for urgent intervention.

timing.description: Any time; separate from the specific C05 / C06.

confirmation: Medical assessment and red-flag / CO2 / blood-pressure check
recommended_steps: Record time / intensity and repeat BP.

medication.summary: Painkiller only per mission SOP, without an arbitrary dose.

do_not: Do NOT mask serious symptoms with an analgesic.
Do NOT automatically attribute it to CO2 / microgravity.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Acute stress
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR / blood pressure may rise non-specifically and are NOT diagnostic. Temperature / CO2 / SpO2 check other causes.
typical_symptoms: Sudden distress / fear / tension after an event
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Reported acute distress / stressful event -> private CHECK-IN; dangerous behavior / suicidal risk -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 self-report is enough for support; not an automatic psychiatric diagnosis.

timing.description: Linked to a stressful event; any time.

recommended_steps: Temporarily reduce workload / remove from the hazard.

medication.summary: No automatic medication or sedative.

do_not: Do NOT diagnose stress from tachycardia.
Do NOT administer benzodiazepines autonomously.
Do NOT share private data without a clear safety reason.

incidence.summary: No specific verified NASA probability for exactly this definition.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: NASA HRP behavioral risk, not a specific CliFF for acute stress.

source.reference: NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF

data_handling.note: Private check-in; do not disclose data without a clear safety reason.

diagnostic_rules.name: Adjustment disorder / adjustment reaction
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No reliable diagnosis from HR/BP/SpO2/CO2/temperature/dose.
typical_symptoms: Impaired daily functioning after an identifiable change / stressor
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Distress + stressful event + impaired functioning -> referral for assessment, NOT an automatic confirmed diagnosis.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 3 factors to request a clinical assessment, not a diagnosis.

timing.description: Linked to an event / change; duration is assessed clinically.

confirmation: Structured psychiatric / psychological assessment and exclusion of another disorder
recommended_steps: Adjust duties and monitor with the CMO.

medication.summary: Drugs only if a specific indication emerges from a specialist; no automated dose.

do_not: Do NOT infer a psychiatric diagnosis from pulse variability.
Do NOT use a sedative without assessment.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Anxiety / panic attack

escalation.when: Red flags: low SpO2, chest pain or syncope.

diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: HR elevated, possibly BP elevated, but non-specific. A normal SpO2 does NOT exclude a serious cause. No diagnostic threshold.

supporting_signals.purpose: Low value is a red flag; normal does not exclude a serious cause

diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Intense fear AND >=1 accompanying symptom -> SUSPECTED after excluding medical causes; low SpO2 / chest pain / syncope -> URGENT.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 accompanying findings only to surface the possibility; not a diagnostic criterion.

timing.description: Any time; attacks may have abrupt onset.

confirmation: Exclude hypoxia, cardiac cause, high CO2 and drug effects
recommended_steps: Check for an organic emergency cause.

medication.summary: Anxiolytic or long-term therapy ONLY per a medical plan (QT, respiratory depression, interactions). No dosage is defined.

do_not: Do NOT call every dyspnea / tachycardia a panic attack.
Do NOT give a sedative if hypoxia or unexplained respiratory failure is present.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Cognitive disturbance
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: SpO2/CO2/BP/temperature: search for possible causes, NOT a measure of cognitive function. Radiation: exposure is not proof of cognitive deficit.

supporting_signals.purpose: Search for possible causes (fever needs core temperature)
Context only; exposure is not proof of cognitive deficit
Context only; exposure is not proof of cognitive deficit
Context only; exposure is not proof of cognitive deficit

diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Sudden confusion / new disorientation -> EMERGENCY even without an abnormal measurement; subacute performance decline -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 acute neurological red flag is enough for urgent assessment.

timing.description: Any time; record acute vs gradual onset.

confirmation: Check organic causes (oxygenation, CO2, glucose with EXTRA kit, fever, stroke, medications) + a validated cognitive test

medication.summary: No automatic psychoactive drug. Specific treatment only based on a confirmed cause.

do_not: Do NOT attribute sudden confusion to fatigue or stress without excluding a medical emergency.
Do NOT automate sedation.

incidence.summary: NASA HRR: risk of cognitive / behavioral changes; no specific verified incidence for the general term 'cognitive disturbance'.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: No dedicated CliFF for this broad code. NASA HRR cognitive risk.

source.reference: NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF

diagnostic_rules.name: Insomnia / sleep disturbance / circadian misalignment
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No automated sleep-duration measurement among the 6 available sensors. HR is not an accurate sleep estimate.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Frequent nighttime sleep problems + daytime effect -> MONITOR / questionnaire. A diary / interview is necessary.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 2 elements (sleep problem + impact), not clinical confirmation.

timing.description: Any time; record over consecutive days; not exclusively early in flight.

confirmation: Actigraphy if available (not one of the six)
recommended_steps: Check shifts, light, noise and CO2.
CBT-I by a specialist where feasible.

medication.summary: Hypnotics / melatonin only if pre-approved. No universal NASA dose is documented for all cases.

do_not: Do NOT automatically give a sedative before a critical task.
Do NOT diagnose a circadian disorder from HR alone.

incidence.summary: No numerical probability verified specifically for Mars DRM; no arbitrary percentage introduced.

diagnostic_rules.name: Interpersonal conflict (crew / Earth / family)
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No biometric diagnostic threshold. HR/BP cannot prove conflict.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Explicit report of conflict / need for support -> TEAM SUPPORT EVENT. Threat of violence / danger -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 report is enough to offer support. NOT A MEDICAL DIAGNOSIS.

timing.description: Any time, possibly with increased workload / isolation.

confirmation: Mediation with consent, privacy and safety assessment

medication.summary: No medication: not a diagnosis that justifies therapy.

do_not: It is FORBIDDEN to apply an automatic psychiatric label or give medication because of a disagreement.
Protect personal data.
medical_kit: Approved team-support mechanism (no mandatory pharmaceutical kit)

incidence.summary: There is no medical disease probability; this is an operational / team risk, not condition-specific incidence.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: Conflict is not a disease. Use a non-medical event code and a separate privacy policy.

source.reference: NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF

data_handling.note: Use a non-medical event code and a separate privacy policy.

diagnostic_rules.name: Mood disturbance / irritability
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: No specific biometric limit from the six sensors. HR/BP changes are non-specific.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Mood change -> private MONITOR / check-in; suicidal ideation / dangerous behavior -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: 1 self-report for support, not a diagnosis. 1 immediate sign of risk for emergency.

timing.description: Any time; record duration and impact.

recommended_steps: Clinical referral if it persists or affects functioning.

medication.summary: No antidepressant / sedative without a full psychiatric diagnosis and a specialized mission SOP.

do_not: Do NOT infer 'depression' from irritability or palpitations.
Do NOT automatically give an SSRI / benzodiazepine.

incidence.summary: No verified frequency for the broad term 'mood disturbance' without a specific diagnostic code.

diagnostic_rules.limitations: 'Mood change' is a symptom; depression requires clinical criteria and a specific CliFF.

source.reference: NASA HRP / related source, not a dedicated CliFF

diagnostic_rules.name: Low Hemoglobin / Anemia
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (CBC). Requires terrestrial-style analysis or i-STAT.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Low Hemoglobin OR Low Hematocrit OR Low RBC -> SUSPECTED. Escalate if severe bleeding signs.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: Any 1 marker below caution limit.

timing.description: Routine blood panel assessment or symptom-driven.

confirmation: Check iron, ferritin, B12, and folic acid.

medication.summary: Supplementation per findings (iron, B12).

do_not: Do not give iron supplements without confirming deficiency.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.

diagnostic_rules.name: High Hemoglobin / Polycythemia
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (CBC).
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: High Hemoglobin OR High Hematocrit OR High RBC -> SUSPECTED.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: Any 1 marker above caution limit.

timing.description: Routine blood panel assessment.

recommended_steps: Investigate for chronic hypoxia or primary polycythemia.

medication.summary: None typically required; hydration is key.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.

diagnostic_rules.name: Leukopenia / Neutropenia (Low WBC)
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (CBC). Watch core_temperature closely.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Low WBC OR Low Neutrophils OR Low Lymphocytes -> SUSPECTED. If accompanied by fever -> EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: Any 1 marker below caution limit.

red_flags.description: Fever with severe neutropenia is a medical emergency requiring immediate antibiotics.

timing.description: Routine blood panel.

confirmation: Assess immune status and infection risk.
recommended_steps: Administer antibiotics immediately if fever develops.

medication.summary: Broad-spectrum antibiotics for febrile neutropenia per mission SOP.

do_not: Do not ignore a fever in a neutropenic patient.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.

diagnostic_rules.name: Leukocytosis / Neutrophilia (High WBC)
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (CBC).
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: High WBC OR High Neutrophils -> SUSPECTED (Infection/Inflammation).
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: Any 1 marker above caution limit.

timing.description: Routine blood panel or symptom-driven.

confirmation: Investigate underlying cause (bacterial infection, acute inflammation).

medication.summary: Antibiotics only if a bacterial infection is confirmed or highly suspected.

do_not: Do not give antibiotics merely for an elevated WBC without clinical correlation.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.

diagnostic_rules.name: Thrombocytopenia (Low Platelets)
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (CBC).
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: Low Platelets -> SUSPECTED. Bleeding signs -> URGENT/EMERGENCY.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: Platelets below caution limit.

red_flags.description: Active bleeding (e.g., uncontrolled_bleeding) in a patient with low platelets is a critical emergency.

timing.description: Routine blood panel.

confirmation: Repeat measurement to rule out lab error.
recommended_steps: Stop antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications if applicable.

medication.summary: Specific hematological treatment per ground specialist.

do_not: Do not administer aspirin or NSAIDs.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.

diagnostic_rules.name: Elevated D-dimer / VTE Risk
diagnostic_rules.sensor_notes: Detected via blood panel (lipid profile/D-dimer assay). Ultrasound is mandatory for confirmation.
diagnostic_rules.logic_description: High D-dimer -> URGENT assessment for blood clots.
diagnostic_rules.minimum_criteria: D-dimer above caution limit.

red_flags.description: Elevated D-dimer with chest pain or hypoxia requires immediate PE evaluation.

timing.description: Any time, especially post-flight or during long missions.

recommended_steps: Ultrasound of suspected area (usually lower limbs or jugular in space).
Do not rely solely on D-dimer for diagnosis.
Anticoagulant therapy only if thrombosis is documented or highly suspected clinically.

medication.summary: Anticoagulants per physician order.

do_not: Do not start anticoagulation based solely on an elevated D-dimer without imaging or strong clinical signs.

incidence.summary: Not specified in CliFFs.
